subject: Brokered capacity allocation — Helio AI tri-region activation and node-commit cadence
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.example>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brokered capacity allocation — Helio AI tri-region activation and node-commit cadence

Team —

Helio just signed the SOW (attached v3) but they want an activation timeline that guarantees tri-region Dedicated pools: US (primary), EU (latency), APAC (pilot Singapore). This is a deal-led ask tied to a 12-month reserved commitment (deal HLIO-2026-49). Sales wants a clear nodal commitment schedule we can publish to Procurement so they can start internal approvals.

High-level ask: propose a staggered node-commit cadence (numbers per region, pre-warm policy, burst windows) and identify any risk that would require contractual guardrails (e.g., minimum lead times, prepayment for capacity backstop). Helio's estimated peak Q1 load is ~120 sustained A100-equivalent GPUs across the three regions, with burst to 200 for 48-hour launches.

Please include:
- A suggested initial committed split (US/EU/APAC) and where burst capacity will come from.
- Any operational constraints (e.g., cross-region replication windows, capacity warm-up time).
- A short list of mitigations if inventory is tight in APAC.

I copied Laura for pricing/commit impact and Stephanie for contracting. I'm hoping to push a single schedule back to Sam (Helio) by EOD tomorrow so Procurement can circulate.

Thanks — Rafa

--
Rafael Mendes
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.example
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.example>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Brokered capacity allocation — Helio AI tri-region activation and node-commit cadence

Rafa / team —

Thanks — ran a quick sketch with infra on sizing. Summary recommendations below (will attach CSV with TTL-per-region math):

1) Initial committed split (month 0 activation):
   - US (primary): 70 A100-equivalent GPUs (sustained)
   - EU: 30 A100-equivalent GPUs (sustained)
   - APAC (SG pilot): 20 A100-equivalent GPUs (sustained)
   -> total committed baseline = 120 GPUs (matches Helio estimate).

2) Burst/fallback plan:
   - Burst buffer: reserve 80 GPUs in a pooled surge lane that can be routed to any region within 3–6 hours (capacity depending on cloud/backfill availability). This yields theoretical burst capacity to 200.
   - If APAC physical inventory is constrained, we recommend routing APAC burst to nearby SG edge + warm standby in JP region (if available) and use lower-precision quantized variants for burst traffic to preserve latency.

3) Warm-up & lead times:
   - Node pre-warm: 48–72 hours for cache warm-up and model weights; recommend 72 hours for initial ramp to avoid cold-start QPS drops.
   - Procurement commit to a 14-day minimum notice for guaranteed node provisioning; same-day burst is best-effort and subject to cross-region capacity.

4) Operational constraints / mitigations:
   - Cross-region KV cache: acceptable but expect ~1–3% tail latency increase when falling back to remote pools for large KV cache miss rates.
   - APAC scarcity mitigation: propose a 2-tranche onboarding where APAC committed increases by +10 GPUs at month 3 if utilization > 65% over a 14-day window; otherwise we keep APAC at baseline and run burst off US/EU with quantized model fallback.

5) SLA/contract ask to protect Redwood:
   - Include a rolling review every 90 days to re-baseline committed nodes tied to observed token throughput and 30-day notice for any downscale below baseline.

I'll attach the estimated-node-plan.csv with regional ramp week-by-week. If this looks good, we can send to Sam with an outline for the SOW activation table.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Capacity Planning
karthik_iyer@redwood.example

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 01:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Brokered capacity allocation — Helio AI tri-region activation and node-commit cadence

Rafael / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement shared a few questions (inline):

> 1) We need a firm activation date per region for our internal change window (Helio runs major releases every quarter). Can you provide target activation weeks?
>
> 2) What happens to unused committed capacity in months with low traffic? Do we receive credits?
>
> 3) We require an explicit fallback policy for APAC in case physical inventory prevents provisioning within 30 days.

Answers from our side would be great; Procurement also wants the DocuSign link and SOW with the node table so finance can sign off. We're aiming for activation in early Jan if possible. Attached: Procurement_Checklist.pdf (we'll email a signed SOW after your final table).

Sam
Head of Ops, Helio AI
sam@helio.ai

Subject: Re: Brokered capacity allocation — Helio AI tri-region activation and node-commit cadence

Sam / team —

Quick answers to Procurement items (high level):

1) Activation weeks:
   - US: target week of 2027-01-04 (can prioritize earlier if Helio approves ramp fees).
   - EU: target week of 2027-01-11.
   - APAC (SG pilot): target week of 2027-01-18 (subject to inventory confirmation).

2) Unused committed capacity:
   - Standard reserved model: month-to-month committed fee applies; we offer a utilization credit program where >80% utilization in a quarter yields token-credit rebates applied to the following quarter. We can include a contracted credit schedule in SOW (example in attached SOW_v3).

3) APAC fallback policy:
   - If physical nodes cannot be provisioned into APAC within 30 days of the contracted activation date, Redwood will: (a) provide equivalent sustained capacity via EU/US routing gates with latency SLAs defined for fallback; (b) apply a one-time operational credit for inability to meet the APAC activation date; (c) commit to a 30-day remediation plan to bring APAC to baseline or provide permanent routing if Helio agrees.

I've attached a redline-ready SOW (Helio_SOW_v3.pdf) and a DocuSign activation link (docusign-activation-link.txt). Laura, please confirm pricing impacts of the burst buffer and the 80 GPU pooled surge pricing.

- Stephanie

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Contracts & Pricing, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example

Subject: Re: Brokered capacity allocation — Helio AI tri-region activation and node-commit cadence

Sam / Maya / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick feedback. To keep timelines tight, summary action items and commitments below: 

- Activation targets: US 2027-01-04 | EU 2027-01-11 | APAC 2027-01-18 (provisional; final after inventory check).
- Committed baseline: 70US / 30EU / 20APAC = 120 GPUs. Burst pool: 80 pooled GPUs (routeable; best-effort within 3–6 hours).
- If APAC cannot be provisioned within 30 days of the target we will route traffic to EU/US and issue the agreed operational credit.
- Stephanie to include utilization-credit schedule in SOW; Laura to confirm pricing and add the burst buffer line item.
- Helio to sign SOW and DocuSign activation link once node table is final (we sent CSV: estimated-node-plan.csv).

I'll follow up after Laura confirms costs — planning to send a single consolidated activation table to Procurement by COB Friday.

Thanks everyone —
Rafael
